config.title: W2 가지 출력의 추론 시 축소 진단
config.question: Is the RR2 shortfall of W2 (43 C2) caused by the W2 branch output itself, and does the extra RR2 error sit in frequencies the MS observation cannot see?

models.C2_alpha: 43 C2 best, seeds 42-44; backbone output = original(x) + alpha * branch(x) at inference only

tests.RR2: RR scenes degraded once more, GT = RR MS
tests.FR_WALD: FR scenes degraded once, GT = FR MS
tests.FR_OBS: interior observation RMSE of FR output (DN)

config.error_split: per test, error e = prediction - GT; low = SensorObservation(QB).blur(e) (MTF low-pass, the band the MS observation sees); high = e - low; RMSE in DN over the full image
config.protocol: common/evaluation_protocol.py (WaldDegradation, predict, rr_metrics, observation_rmse); FP32 inference, float64 metrics

readout.H1_branch_causes_RR2_loss: seed-mean RR2 PSNR decreases from alpha=0 to alpha=1 while RR PSNR increases (monotone trend over the 5 alphas)
readout.H2_unobservable_band: the RR2 error increase from alpha=0 to 1 is larger in the high band than in the low band (RMSE_high delta > RMSE_low delta)
readout.alpha_one_check: alpha=1 reproduces the experiment 47 C2 values (RR PSNR within 0.001 dB)

not_allowed: choosing alpha on test as a model change (diagnostic only; no adoption)
config.execution: single low-priority evaluation process on the 48/49 server; 49 training numerics are unaffected (separate process), throughput is shared for the run time
